transitions.summary: Benevolent government aligns ceremonial signs with the seasons, allowing public life to settle into care, sufficiency, and freedom from immediate worry.
A mother responds to her crying young and seeks nourishment, yet returns to an empty nest where devoted care can no longer reach its object.
Empty hands and repeated falls do not end the movement; recovery follows each descent until the situation opens toward abundance and peace.
The heavenly pivot and dipper take their ordered places, making pattern, measure, and coordinated restraint the basis of harmony and joy.
Cultivated character and kindness gather blessing around the household and realm, joining ethical power with peace and material well-being.
Private rivalry and predatory desire spread through a ruined political order until partnership, family continuity, and the ruling clan are all destroyed.
Monstrous and headless figures surround a fleeing spirit that can find no place to settle, portraying complete disorientation after identity and center dissolve.
Imperial levels remain inaccessible to ordinary people, while rulers cannot be seen across the height, expressing distance created by rigid hierarchy.
A richly adorned bird travels north to meet a sage ruler, and the encounter coincides with harvest, gladness, and freedom from banditry.
A soft blade cannot shape resistant jade, and repeated effort only callouses the hands when the tool lacks the capacity the work requires.
Great value rises from an obscure valley into visible height, where its radiance can illuminate the country and become publicly useful.
A valued companion is carried away, but fear prevents effective pursuit; the one left behind returns alone with the loss unresolved.
A wandering animal returns to its proper bounds and its keeper comes home, turning recovered belonging into a condition without further concern.
Tyranny and chaos become matters of collective concern, prompting organized force and the search for worthy authority capable of restoring limits.
Appointment raises a capable person into visible service, and favor from above allows the new position to radiate benefit.
A high power descends and brothers are called into duty, where the burden of service is accompanied by recognition and secure standing.
A vulnerable animal enters cultivated ground and hears a predator’s roar, yet the immediate terror subsides without becoming lasting disaster.
Boats drift across boundless water without roots or secure mooring, leaving the heart anxious because movement lacks any stable point of return.
A little grain saves a starving traveler, and the timely gift establishes a bond of gratitude capable of returning help later.
Abuse of position exhausts favor until rank disappears and the former holder is reduced to ordinary service under others.
A fox chase reaches a barrier too deep to cross, and the desired capture remains beyond reach because the terrain itself blocks progress.
The wild landscape contains animals but no cultivated community, and what is present cannot fulfill ceremonial need, leaving grief amid unusable abundance.
Terror and obstruction reinforce one another until even a single step becomes impossible, turning anticipated danger into complete immobility.
The young fox wets its tail before finishing the crossing, gaining no material advantage while still moving in accord with the larger way.
Precious court objects accompany the image of impoverished counselors raised into service, suggesting that neglected ability can find a fitting public role.
A journey through a difficult gate secures standing and resources, receives distant favor, and completes its arc in a restorative return home.
A bird sways on a slender reed and cannot settle comfortably, yet the strain remains contained and does not develop into full disaster.
Like the pole star within its palace, ordered appearance and benevolent power establish a stable center from which repeated blessing can spread.
A tyrant consumes the people’s strength until defeat, revolt, and death overturn the very authority that enabled the excess.
Spinning and weaving continue in isolation after complementary relationship has broken, making necessary work the emblem of a severed and diminished life.
Service to the ruler pulls labor away from the fields, so public obligation leaves the agricultural foundation untended and without harvest.
Work in the fields unexpectedly comes within sight of the ruler’s tower, suggesting a transition from obscure cultivation toward recognized service.
Auspicious creatures rest where a noble person teaches the people, joining humane education with a stable civic environment.
Disordered weaving leaves ceremonial clothing unfinished, but hearing the warning in time checks the difficulty before it becomes complete disaster.
Repeated attempts to dodge danger provide no secure route and steadily consume resources, leaving the traveler worried and poorly supplied.
Hobbled movement and opposed speech prevent advancement, while the unbloomed lotus marks a condition whose development has not yet reached its time.
A failing horse and depleted attendants cannot carry the traveler home, so return is postponed by the weakness of the whole supporting system.
Marriage, blossom, and long blessing unfold within a military setting, where a young person’s life also rises toward noble recognition.
Loss of sight, hearing, and speech separates action from understanding and response, so effort proceeds without producing meaningful accomplishment.
Virtues, phases, seasons, and complementary forces take their proper sequence, allowing the country to settle into health and security.
Mutiny and disorder dissolve the army’s organizing center, and the violence spreads into households as plunder, hunger, and cold.
Leaves cover the eyes until even siblings disappear from view, and chosen or imposed blindness leaves the solitary figure separated from worthy company.
Fire is attempted in water and fishing on a summit, so neither activity can produce its intended result under conditions wholly unsuited to it.
A mountain fortress confronts descending water that cannot be permanently held, and the pressure eventually opens doors that confinement had closed.
Long legs move slowly yet cover immense distance, while expert guidance and judgment support a successful journey toward a distant source of favor.
An eclipse portrays the upper power obscuring and damaging what depends upon it, while the historical image shows leadership forced into exile.
Young auspicious creatures inhabit a good realm where harmony, health, and the presence of wise people make collective life thrive.
A crane settles where fields and ponds are abundant, and one well-placed trap gathers a double benefit from the same environment.
